1Signing in

DocBingo is a web application: nothing to install. Open https://docbingo.ch (or www.docbingo.ch, docbingo.com) in a browser (computer, tablet or smartphone), enter your email and password and click Sign in. The login is remembered on the device; the button with your name, top right, lets you sign out. You land on the Home page: session in progress to resume, questions to review, key figures, latest sessions and quick actions.

After 15 minutes without use, the server goes to sleep. The first load can then take up to a minute — this is normal. As long as the application stays open, it remains responsive. Open DocBingo five minutes before a session.

1bAccounts, roles and question review

DocBingo distinguishes two roles. The administrator (you) publishes directly, validates proposals, manages accounts and settings. Authors (colleagues, residents…) create questions and propose them; they only enter sessions once published by an administrator.

  1. Create an account: Settings → User accounts → name, email, role → Create account. A temporary password is displayed: pass it on; the person will have to change it at their first login (Settings → My account).
  2. Author side: in the question form, two buttons — Save as draft (visible to them only) or Submit for review. Their questions carry a Draft / Proposed badge in their list.
  3. Administrator side: a To review tab appears with the number of pending proposals. For each one: Publish, or Return it as a draft with a comment the author will see when reopening the question.
  4. Resetting a password (🔑) or deactivating an account (⏸) is done from the same list. Users can also click Forgot password? on the login screen: a link valid for one hour is emailed to them (if email sending is configured on the installation).
A question that was published and then edited by an author goes back to “proposed”: nothing changes in sessions until you have validated it again.

2Building the question bank

The bank is the heart of DocBingo: the richer it is, the more varied the sessions will be. The Questions tab lists all questions, with a search box and a keyword filter (click one or more #keywords; with several, choose OR / AND).

Creating a question

  1. Click ＋ New question.
  2. Enter the statement. If a very similar question already exists, an alert is shown to avoid duplicates.
  3. Fill in 2 to 5 options (A to E). Click the letter to mark the correct answer(s) (it turns green). Several correct answers are possible: participants will then have to write all the letters, for example “BD”.
  4. If needed, add an illustration (ECG, X-ray, photo — resized automatically) and a teaching explanation: it is shown to the audience together with the answer.
  5. Choose the difficulty level (easy / medium / hard): it will be used to balance or order sessions.
  6. Optionally attach the question to a clinical case (existing, or created on the fly with a title) and set its order within the case: questions of the same case will always be asked consecutively, in that order.
  7. Add one or more keywords (type, then Enter; existing keywords are suggested). They are what will let you build sessions by theme.
  8. Save.
Use consistent keywords (a specialty, a cross-cutting theme: #emergency, #ecg…). A question can have several. Duplicate lets you quickly create a variant of an existing question.
Questions already used display “used 1×”: when creating a session, you will be able to exclude questions that have already been asked.

Author, AI provenance, bulk editing and trash

Every question keeps its author's name (the account signed in when it was created or imported) — shown in the bank and the form, never on participants' screens. A question produced by AI generation additionally carries the 🤖 AI mark and automatically receives the #ia keyword, so it can be found or filtered. In the bank, tick one or more questions (or Select all) to add or remove keywords in bulk. The 🗑 button moves a question, after confirmation, to the Trash: it is no longer offered in the bank nor used to build a session, but stays recoverable (Restore) until the trash is emptied permanently with the dedicated button.

2bImporting or generating questions

Questions tab → ⬆ Import. Three routes, all leading to the same editable preview: you proofread, correct, untick what does not fit, then save. Duplicates are skipped automatically.

📄 File
CSV or Excel (one question per row: Statement, A, B, C, D, E, Correct answer, Explanation, Keywords, Difficulty — download the CSV template), Word (.docx) or plain text.
📝 Pasted text
One block per question, separated by a blank line: the statement, then A) … B) …, a line Answer: B (or ABC), and optionally Explanation: …, Difficulty: easy, #cardiology.

✨ Generate with AI

Paste a source text (article, guideline, lecture notes), state the number of questions wanted, the level and keywords: the AI drafts MCQs with explanations, which you review and validate just like an import — nothing enters the bank without your approval. This feature requires an Anthropic API key entered in Settings (indicative cost: a few cents per batch); without a key it stays inactive.

The AI is a writing assistant, not a medical reference: check every statement, every correct answer and every explanation before validating — this is precisely why the editable preview is mandatory.

3Creating a session

Sessions tab → ＋ New session. The form guides you, and the preview on the right updates live with automatic checks.

SettingWhat it does
Question selectionRandom from the whole bank, or by theme (one or more keywords). Tick “exclude questions already used” to keep things fresh.
SizingBy number of questions or by target duration (the software computes the number of questions from the time per question, allowing about 15 s for showing the answer).
Time / questionLength of the countdown before the answer is shown automatically (60 s by default; adjustable live while running the session).
ParticipantsNumber of cards to generate (+ 10 % spares, minimum 2).
DifficultyAny, Balanced (one third of each level), Progressive (from easy to hard), or a single level. Clinical cases always stay grouped and in order.
ParticipationPaper + phone (default: everyone chooses), Paper only (no session code) or Phone only (digital cards for everyone, printing optional as a backup). See § 6c.
Marking modeCorrect answer required: the participant writes their answer in the cell and only ticks it if it is right (“serious game” mode). Pure luck: the cell is ticked as soon as the number is drawn (relaxed mode, guaranteed winner).
After a first bingoContinue or end — just a default value, you decide live when the bingo happens.
Card sizeAuto: DocBingo simulates thousands of games and recommends 3×3, 4×4 or 5×5 so that a first bingo occurs around 70 % of the way through the session. You can force a size.
Spaced repetitionCheckbox: questions with a low success rate (phone answers) are drawn first — to revisit what was missed in previous sessions.
Thematic cardsCheckbox: choose as many keywords as there are rows (3, 4 or 5); each row of the card only contains questions from its theme (“the cardio row”). Questions are asked theme by theme.
Effects, notesSounds and animations for this session; personal notes visible only in the presenter console.
A red alert (not enough questions) blocks creation: reduce the number of questions, broaden the keywords or create questions. A yellow alert is just a warning.

Click Create the session and generate the cards. The questions are drawn at random and frozen for this session; the unique cards are generated and numbered (G-001, G-002…).

3bFine-tuning a session: order, slides

As long as the session has not been started, the detail page lets you adjust the running order: click ✎ Edit order.

  1. ↑ ↓ move a question; 🎲 Shuffle redraws the order at random.
  2. ⟳ replaces a question with another one, drawn at random from the same selection (same keywords) — handy to set aside a question already seen.
  3. ＋ Insert a slide adds a free screen between two questions: a part title (“Part two: emergencies”), a break (“Coffee break — back in 10 minutes”) or a clinical case introduction. While running the session, the slide is shown on the public display, the countdown is suspended, and you resume with one click (or from the remote control).
Reordering or replacing questions changes nothing on cards already printed: they only depend on the draw numbers, not on the content of the questions.

4Printing the cards

The session detail page summarises the settings, the draw order of the questions and the ⬇ Download the cards PDF button.

  1. Download the PDF and print it on A4 paper, portrait, 100 % scale (no fit-to-page).
  2. Each sheet holds two cards separated by a dotted line: cut with a guillotine — you get A5-sized cards.
  3. Hand out one card per participant. Keep the spare cards for latecomers. Bring pens!
Each card carries a code (e.g. G-014) at the top right: this is the code the participant will call out in case of a bingo. The rules are printed on every card as a reminder.

5On the day: setting up the room

With a projector (recommended)
Connect the projector in “extend display” mode (not mirror). Open DocBingo, start the session, click 🖥️ Open the public display: a new window opens — drag it onto the projected screen and switch it to full screen (F11). Your own screen becomes the presenter console.
Single screen
Simply start the session: the public display and the controls (bar at the bottom) are on the same screen. Ideal for a small group or with a single TV screen.
Open DocBingo 5 minutes ahead (server wake-up), test the projector sound with the 👁 Answer button on the first question, then go back with ⏮ if needed.

6Running the session

From the session list, click ▶ Run. The introduction screen recaps the settings. Click ▶ Start the first question or press Space.

How a question unfolds

  1. The number appears in large type (draw animation): participants look for it on their card.
  2. The question and the options are displayed; the countdown runs (red under 10 s).
  3. At zero, the correct answer is shown automatically in green with the explanation. You can reveal it earlier (👁 Answer) or grant more time (＋15 s).
  4. ⏭ Next (or Space) moves to the next question. The drawn numbers strip fills up at the bottom.

The presenter console (dual screen)

The console shows what the audience cannot see: the correct answer and the explanation, the next question, your notes, the progress and estimated remaining time, and the Session panel with the counter of cards “still in the running” (can be hidden). The small 🖥️ at the top right lights up when the public display is connected.

CommandKeyboardEffect
Pause / ResumePSuspends the countdown (for a digression, a question from the audience…).
＋15 s—Extends the thinking time.
AnswerSpaceReveals the answer immediately.
NextSpace / →Next question (after the answer).
Previous←Go back to the previous question (answer shown).
Verify a bingo—Opens the verification (pauses the countdown).
Continue (slide)SpaceCloses the free slide being shown and resumes the running order.
Autosave. The session state is saved at every question. In case of a crash, a power cut or an accidental close, reopen DocBingo: a green banner “Resume the session in progress” takes you back exactly where you were.

6bThe smartphone remote control

To run the session while moving around the room: the presenter console shows a 📱 Remote control panel with an address and a 4-digit code. On your smartphone, open the address (or scan it), enter the code: you get the Previous, Pause, +15 s, Answer, Next and Verify a bingo commands (with card code entry). Each command acts instantly on the console — and therefore on the projected screen.

The code changes with every session; the ⟳ button generates a new one if needed. The remote control does not need the DocBingo password — the code is enough — but it cannot do anything other than drive the session.

6cThe voting pad: participants on smartphones

Depending on the session's Participation setting (paper, phone or both), participants can play on their smartphone in addition to or instead of paper cards. The introduction screen and the public display show the address to open and a 6-character session code; everyone enters their first name and receives a digital card (or declares the code of their paper card to follow it on screen).

Participant side
At each question, they tap their answer (A–E; for multiple answers, they tick then submit). They then see whether it is right, the explanation, the distribution of the room's answers, and their card is ticked automatically according to the session rule. When a line is complete, the bingo is detected and announced automatically — nothing left to verify.
Presenter side
The console shows the number of connected participants, how many have answered, and after the answer the A–E distribution (also projected on the public display). Each correct answer earns 100 points, plus a speed bonus; the leaderboard builds up live and a podium closes the session.
Both modes coexist within the same session: some play on paper (verification by card code, § 7), others on smartphone (fully automatic). A participant who has a paper card can also declare it on their phone to follow it on screen.
Answers received via smartphone feed the statistics (§ 8b): success rate per question and per keyword, most missed questions.

6dBonus question and jokers

After an answer has been shown, the ⚡ Bonus button launches a flash question outside the session (drawn from the bank): participants on smartphones answer it; a correct answer gives them a joker — a free cell to tick wherever they like on their card (🃏 button on their phone). You reveal the answer, then close the bonus to resume the running order. An ideal moment of suspense at the halfway point.

7Verifying a bingo

A participant shouts “Bingo!”: ask for their card code, click 🎉 Verify a bingo and enter the code (“G-014” or simply “14”).

“Correct answer required” mode
DocBingo shows the card with the cells of the questions already asked, flags the complete lines and lists, for each of them, the correct answer of every cell. Compare with the letters written in pen on the paper card: if everything is right, Validate the bingo.
“Pure luck” mode
Verification is fully automatic: the software knows which numbers have been drawn. A complete line = bingo, validate.

On validation: confetti, jingle, announcement on the public display — then DocBingo offers to continue the session (further winners are possible) or to end it. If no line is complete, the bingo is invalid: “Close and resume”.

8End of session and history

After the last question (or on “End”), the final screen shows the winners and the number of questions asked. In “correct answer required” mode, if there was no bingo, the fallback rule applies: the winner is the one with the most ticked cells (ties broken by a tie-break question or a draw).

⧉ Duplicate recreates a session with the same settings but new questions and new cards — perfect for a new cohort. Tick “exclude questions already used” to guarantee fresh content.

8bStatistics and summary sheet

The Statistics tab aggregates all answers given via smartphone: overall success rate, most missed questions (worth revisiting in class… or rewording), success per keyword, bingo hall of fame, and the table of all assessed questions.

In the detail of a finished session, the Results block offers the summary sheet (PDF): all questions in order, the correct answer in green, the explanation, the room's success rate and the podium — a revision handout to give to participants.

8cSharing question collections

Settings → Collections: export a file containing the published questions of one or more keywords (images and clinical cases included) and pass it on to another department, another hospital or another DocBingo instance; conversely, import a received collection — duplicates are skipped, and the questions arrive with the status matching your role. It is also a good way to back up a topic.

9Settings: language, theme, effects

The Settings tab lets you choose the visual theme (Swiss precision — default, Clinical neon, Vitamin pop), the interface language (French, English, German — including the rules printed on the cards), turn sounds and animations on or off, and pick the sound ambience (Classic, TV quiz, Zen, Casino — Listen button to compare). This is also where you enter the API key for AI generation, and where the 📖 Open the presenter guide button (this document) lives. These settings are remembered.

Backup: the Export the question bank (JSON) button downloads your whole bank. Do it regularly and keep the file somewhere safe — it is months of your work.

10Rules to explain to participants

“Correct answer required” mode
  1. A number is shown: look for it on your card.
  2. If you have it, write your answer (A–E) in the cell before the countdown ends. Several letters if several correct answers.
  3. When the solution is shown: right → tick the cell; wrong → cross it out (lost).
  4. Complete row, column or diagonal → shout BINGO and give your card code.
“Pure luck” mode
  1. A number is shown: if you have it, tick the cell.
  2. Answer the question anyway — that is the whole point of the game!
  3. Complete row, column or diagonal → BINGO + card code.
State up front what happens after the first bingo (do we go on until the second? until the end?) and the fallback rule (most ticked cells): it avoids arguments.

11Troubleshooting and good practice

SituationWhat to do
The page takes a long time to loadServer wake-up after inactivity (up to 1 min). Be patient; open the application a few minutes before your sessions.
The room wifi drops during the sessionCarry on: the questions and cards are loaded, and console ↔ public display synchronisation goes through the browser itself. Saving will resume when the network is back. Avoid reloading the page while the network is down, though.
The browser closed / the computer rebootedReopen DocBingo → “Resume the session in progress” banner. Reopen the public display from the console (🖥️ Public display button).
The public display does not openThe browser blocked the window: allow pop-ups for docbingo.ch, then click the button again.
No soundCheck that sounds are enabled (Settings and session settings), the browser volume, and click once in the page (browsers require an interaction before playing a sound).
A participant has a card with a number that is not in the sessionImpossible: each card only uses the numbers of its own session. Check that the card really comes from this session (the name is printed at the top).
I want to edit a question after creating a sessionThe edit applies to future sessions; the session already created keeps a frozen copy of its questions (consistency with the printed cards).

Backups

Your data (questions, images, sessions, accounts, statistics) is stored in a database hosted in Europe (Turso, with 24-hour point-in-time restore). In addition, a full encrypted backup is made automatically every week and kept for 90 days in the project's GitHub space (“Actions” → “Weekly backup”). You can also, at any time, download a full backup from Settings → Backup, and restore it from the same place (an operation that replaces all data: it asks you to type RESTAURER). Recommendation: download a full backup after every major data-entry session and keep it offline.

Good practice

Plan for at least twice as many questions in the bank as there are cells on a card so that the cards are clearly different; 40 questions and a 4×4 card are a good format for one hour. Test the readability of the projection from the back of the room: dark themes (Swiss precision in projection, Clinical neon) are the most readable in a dark room, Vitamin pop suits bright rooms. Finally, export the question bank after every big data-entry session.

12Terms of use, demo video, smartphone app

Terms of use. At their first login, every account must read and accept the terms of use (also available from About & legal notice and the footer). They set the legal and ethical framework of DocBingo, in particular: no identifying data in questions and clinical cases (no names, initials, precise dates, places or record numbers), anonymisation of any visual material before uploading, copyright of the images and excerpts used (contribution released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), appropriate and respectful content, mandatory review of AI-generated questions without ever sending patient data to the AI, and compliance with the rules of one's institution and professional body. Authors are solely responsible for their contribution; DocBingo and its creator cannot be held liable for any breach of these rules. The terms also recall the spirit of the game: kindness, a will to teach, no humiliating rankings, inclusive language wherever possible. A reminder is shown at the top of the creation and import forms; until the terms are accepted, creating and importing questions is blocked.

Demo video. From the Home page, the 🎬 Demo video button opens a three-minute guided tour (bank, import and AI, session, running the session with smartphones, presenter mode, statistics, settings), with subtitles and clickable chapters. It is only visible after signing in — handy for showing the tool to a colleague.

On a smartphone: add to the home screen. DocBingo is an installable web application: on a phone or tablet, a banner offers Install (Android/Chrome) or explains the steps on iPhone/iPad (Share button → Add to Home Screen). The DocBingo icon then appears among your apps and opens full screen — ideal for the remote control and the participants' voting pad. The banner can be hidden (it comes back after 30 days).
